- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts show gradual upward drift, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.
- If recent sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and true prices show sharp rebound, adjust forecast to allow for immediate reversal or mean reversion.
- After high-impact auction events (supply net >0), model tends to over-forecast prices; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 3–5 days post-event.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often under- or over-estimates volatility; use median of recent 5-day true price range as anchor.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly but true price spikes sharply, apply “overshoot correction” — reduce forecast by 10–15% for next 3–5 days to avoid lagged reaction.
- In high-event periods (≥15 events/30d), model tends to over-predict price rise; apply “event-adjusted mean reversion” — subtract 1–3% of supply net from forecast baseline.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bearish spikes followed by recovery, model often under-estimates rebound; add 2–5% upward bias to forecast for 3–7 days post-bearish dip.
